assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory turned protein folding from a paradox into a quantitative physical-chemical framework, and the experimental side (phi-value analysis, kinetics, single-molecule work) tested it directly. This is the kind of theory that connects quantitatively to experiment, and it underpins how we now think about folding, misfolding and, indirectly, structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes introduced the funnel/spin-glass picture, Onuchic developed it into predictive structure-based models, Dill shaped the hydrophobic-collapse view, and Fersht supplied the decisive experimental mapping of folding transition states. Three names (Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht) give a theory-plus-experiment configuration, but leaving out Dill and Bryngelson is a real priority cost.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of confirmation across independent theory and experiment groups; the interpretation is stable and widely taught. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature, though the 2024 prize touched adjacent protein structure ground.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or physics/biophysics.
Credit among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Bryngelson is contestable.
Overlap with the 2024 protein prediction/design prize may weigh against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted degradation through PROTACs and molecular glues is a genuine game-changer: a new therapeutic modality with a clear chemical principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) and a rapidly growing clinical pipeline. It opens previously undruggable targets and recasts thalidomide-type drugs mechanistically.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, and others (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito) made decisive later contributions. Three-person limit forces hard choices; Crews, Deshaies and Handa is defensible but not uncontroversial.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic confirmation and many compounds in clinical trials, but approved degrader drugs are still few, so real-world consequences are still developing.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete.
Priority between PROTAC inventors and glue-degrader mechanism discoverers is unresolved.
Ciulli and Gray are left out of the proposed three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a simple, general and reliable reaction that changed how amines and heteroarylamines are made across pharmaceuticals and materials. Its impact is enormous and easy to demonstrate, in the spirit of prizes that reward a straightforward route with broad consequences.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig are the clear leaders with complementary mechanistic and catalyst-design work; Kosugi's early tin-amide coupling is a legitimate precursor and an attribution question, but the cleanest prize is Buchwald and Hartwig. I include Kosugi only as a third name for priority consideration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: forty years of independent use, industrial scale, and 2010 cross-coupling prize already recognized adjacent chemistry, which may argue it has been partly covered.
uncertainties: Possible view that the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize already covers this area.
Kosugi priority versus Buchwald/Hartwig breadth.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines; they have already shown huge real consequences. The key chemical idea, pH-dependent ionizable lipids that encapsulate nucleic acid and release it in endosomes, is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the formulation and ionizable-lipid foundations at UBC; Anderson and Langer drove the combinatorial lipid discovery and delivery in vivo. Attribution is crowded and I cannot claim to have verified exact priority; Cullis is the central figure.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; the mechanism is reasonably understood though endosomal escape details are still debated. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized mRNA modification, not delivery.
uncertainties: Precise division of credit among UBC and MIT/Alnylam groups.
Whether the committee regards this as chemistry or pharmaceutical technology.
Patent and commercial disputes may cloud priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, here via sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators, transformed biology and medicine by collapsing sequencing cost by orders of magnitude. It is a clear game-changer built on chemistry of nucleotides and surfaces.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry; Mayer, Ju and Rothberg contributed alternative or parallel technologies (Ju: reversible terminators; Rothberg: pyrosequencing on beads). A two-person prize is plausible but contested by the other pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and ubiquitous. Sequencing methods were recognized in 1980 and 'Sanger' lineage is already honored, so repeat-field concern exists.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among Solexa, 454 and Ju's reversible terminators.
Possible sense that this belongs to Medicine or to a technology category.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structure and mechanism of nitrogenase, including the iron-molybdenum cofactor and its central carbide, address the central enzyme of biological nitrogen fixation. It is enzymology and bioinorganic chemistry at its most fundamental and links directly to computation of cofactor mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures and cofactor architecture with Dean and others; Einsle established the central carbide and key states; Ribbe and Seefeldt contributed mechanistic and biochemical work. Credit is shared across a large field.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding site remain not fully settled, so interpretation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Unresolved catalytic mechanism.
Broad contributor base makes the three-person limit awkward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made first-principles dynamics practical and opened ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and reactions. It is a landmark of theoretical chemistry with a simple unifying idea (fictitious electron dynamics) and decades of use.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by Car and Parrinello alone, so attribution is unusually clean for a two-person prize. Parrinello also contributed metadynamics and later machine-learning potentials, which may be seen as part of one overall body of work.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with wide independent adoption; arguably the delay is because recognition may have been judged as physics-adjacent or because of the 2013 multiscale and 1998 DFT prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior computational chemistry prizes (1998, 2013).
Whether a combined Parrinello prize with metadynamics or ML potentials would be preferred.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing allows direct, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks and has already reached clinical use. It is original chemistry applied to the genome, with significant consequences.
assessment.attribution: David Liu is the decisive contributor, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees; Kondo and Nishida's cytidine deaminase work was contemporaneous and creates a priority question. A single-laureate prize for Liu is the cleanest, though 2020 CRISPR recognition overlaps in subject.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still early; long-term safety and off-target profile are not fully established, so timing may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Contemporaneous Kondo/Nishida work.
Possible preference for combining with prime editing.
Early clinical evidence.
